target: Recorded positive non-cancelled ordered product units by Order_Date: strip/lowercase statuses, remove exact full-row duplicates, exclude nonpositive Quantity and cancelled orders, retain positive processing and returned orders. No usable return-stock inference. After a key's first source appearance, absent pair-days are zero recorded orders only under an explicit complete-extract assumption; missing demand/capture remains unknown. This fixed target is for comparison to the retained DSC-60 failure, not a newly supplied merchant fact.
baseline: Per-key trailing 91-calendar-day arithmetic mean recorded units times forecast horizon, using only records before target start. This is the fixed 13-week analytical interpretation of the user's recent-months description, not an exact customer incumbent. Do not substitute 84 days or another baseline. Keep all candidates and baseline on identical targets, keys and windows.
primary_metric: Seven-day aggregate mean absolute error in product units per product/store/week, equally weighting all 336 keys and all origins. Lower is better. RMSE, bias, costs, or coverage-horizon scores cannot replace this primary criterion. No business savings/service claim is supported.
population: All 336 Product_ID/Store_ID pairs from the supplied ordering policy. Same population for all candidates and baseline. Disclose static current-assortment retrospective assumptions and undated final-status limitations.
dates: Use target-start Mondays June 30 through September 15, 2025 inclusive for initial selection (12 nonoverlapping seven-day targets), and October 6 through November 24 inclusive for later development check (8). Train strictly before each target start. Both periods are already inspected development. Never access December sales or raw originals. Operational due dates are permitted as-of inputs.
forecast_horizon: Primary: total over seven calendar days starting at each target origin. Deployment orders use supplied supplier lead plus seven-day review; evaluate that mismatch only as a declared secondary diagnostic on fully observable windows. It cannot alter primary selection or the benchmark.
selection_rule: Compare the same six retained candidates: local trailing 28, 91, 182 and 364-calendar-day means; shared patterns; shared seasonal. Shared daily rate is 0.5*local364 mean plus 0.5*network91 daily rate*trailing364 product share*trailing364 store share. Seasonal scales shared by mean future monthly factor/mean trailing91 monthly factor; factors use mean network daily units per month in completed years before origin year, normalized by unweighted mean of 12 month means. Select minimum initial-period primary MAE; within 1e-12 prefer baseline then local28, local182, local364, shared, seasonal. Retain the baseline unless the SAME initial winner improves primary MAE by at least 5% versus baseline in BOTH development periods. Do not promote a different candidate after the later check. This is a predeclared engineering stability rule, not a merchant value threshold or final recording acceptance. No metric switching, target revisions, weaker replacement baseline or repeated tuning; preserve exploratory alternatives separately. Return useful supported baseline results when it wins.
secondary_diagnostics: RMSE, bias, WAPE, origin stability, capture/status sensitivity and fully observed lead-plus-review horizons are diagnostic only. No Data run here can establish performance-success readiness; untouched provenance, frozen parent artifacts, independent final evaluation and preadopted final acceptance remain required. Expected local non-LLM routine running assessment and separate AI-assisted analysis charges must still be explained.
